text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and tool outputs, and the 'inconclusive' leaning with a request for more records is reasonable and cautious. The summary is weakened by a few problems: the cited examples are only two low-complexity claims and do not support the point that the rate is elevated at every level, and the next steps are generic. It also contains an internally inconsistent line and an overstated one.","problems":["Rationale says 'The random charts fully support the billing' immediately before noting 2 of 30 notes with unsupported data review; 'fully' is overstated and self-contradictory.","Headline says 'high at every complexity level' but the tables show 0-complexity share of 7.4% is only modestly above its group baseline; the claim is loosely supported and not cited.","Only two claims are cited, both low-complexity, and they are not paired with any documented chart; the investigator gets no high-complexity or documented examples, nor the 2 claims lacking lab lines.","Next steps are generic: no specific claim IDs to request, no sample size, and no targeting of the 99215 claims in low-complexity patients (21%); 'Re-screen' is vague.","Says 'what came back is too thin' even though 30 of 30 charts were usable and the sample was random, which sits oddly with the earlier statements; the thinness is really that only 6 are 99215.","Does not flag that the documented sample is only 2.4% of claims or that the 6 documented 99215 claims are the relevant evidence base."]}
